resources.string: Add a game or app from your phone. It runs here with its own separate data and sign-in.
Add Google Play services, Play Store and Play Games to %1$s? Games that sign in with Google need them. They run inside the space with their own, separate sign-in.
Google services are in %1$s. Remove them? Games there will no longer be able to sign in with Google.
This phone has no Google Play services to copy into a space.
Clear all data for %1$s in this space? Saved progress and sign-ins stored on the phone will be lost.
Remove %1$s from this space? Its data here will be deleted. The copy installed on your phone is not touched.
Delete %1$s and the data of every app in it?
No matching apps on this phone.
Couldn\'t start %1$s. Try Force stop, then open it again.
The engine didn\'t give a reason.
The engine didn\'t answer. Close Orbit Space, open it again and retry.
That file isn\'t a single installable .apk. Bundles such as .xapk and .apks aren\'t supported: install the app on your phone first, then add it from the list.
No file picker is available on this phone.
This app only has 32-bit code and this is the 64-bit build of Orbit Space. Install the armeabi-v7a build to run it.
This app only has 64-bit code and this is the 32-bit build of Orbit Space. Install the arm64-v8a build to run it.
Your home screen doesn\'t accept pinned shortcuts.
That app couldn\'t be started. It may have been removed from its space.
Applies to apps marked with a dot. Long-press an app on the home screen to turn game mode on or off for it. Changes take effect the next time the app starts.
Free memory before a game starts
Stops every other app running in your spaces.
Ask for the fastest refresh rate
Lets a 90 or 120 Hz screen run at full speed in games.
The screen won\'t dim or lock while a game is open.
Trades peak speed for a steadier frame rate in long sessions. Only some phones support it.
Shows a notification so Android doesn\'t close the engine mid-game. Restart Orbit Space after changing this.
Not granted. Some apps need it to read their files on shared storage. Tap to open the system setting.
Not needed on this version of Android.
No root detected on this phone

Apps in a space run as Orbit Space itself. On a rooted phone, when one of them asks for root your root manager shows the request as coming from Orbit Space, and allowing it gives root to every app in every space. Orbit Space does not fake root on phones that don\'t have it, and does not hide it.
